# How Texas Is Built

> How Texas Is Built is a public education campaign explaining how aggregates and concrete underpin the roads, homes, schools, hospitals, water systems, and infrastructure Texans rely on every day. The site is organized as a five-step journey — Texas is Growing, Economic Impact, Responsible Operations, Local Sourcing, and Quality of Life — following the materials from the state's rapid growth, through the industry's economic impact and environmental oversight, to local supply and the everyday benefits those materials make possible. It is written for Texas residents, policymakers, and media, and is an advocacy initiative of the Texas Aggregates & Concrete Association (TACA).

## Core Pages

- [Home](https://www.howtexasisbuilt.com/): Modern Texas is built on the materials that connect communities, support growth, and strengthen our quality of life.
- [Texas is Growing](https://www.howtexasisbuilt.com/fueling-growth): Texas' favorable business climate continues to drive jobs, investment, and growth — and the materials that make that growth possible.
- [Economic Impact](https://www.howtexasisbuilt.com/jobs): A $10+ billion economic engine supporting more than 100,000 Texas jobs and enabling affordable infrastructure across the state.
- [Responsible Operations](https://www.howtexasisbuilt.com/responsible): Responsible operations, strong communities, and a better Texas for generations to come.
- [Local Sourcing](https://www.howtexasisbuilt.com/local-sourcing): Transportation can account for up to 70% of the delivered cost, which makes local access critical to affordability.
- [Quality of Life](https://www.howtexasisbuilt.com/quality): Shorter commutes, safer roads, affordable homes, reliable water — the everyday benefits Texans rely on, supported by the materials that make them possible.

## Key Facts

- The average home takes 400 tons of aggregates.
- The industry supports more than 100,000 Texas jobs.
- The industry generates more than $10 billion in annual economic activity.
- Every dollar paid in wages creates another $4.95 of earnings in other sectors.
- Every job in the aggregates industry supports nearly six more in the local economy.
- Texas produces over 300 million tons of aggregates every year.
- Texas supplies more than 16% of the entire U.S. ready-mix concrete supply.
- Closed-loop systems used in processes like aggregates washing can recycle roughly 92% to 98% of the water they use.
- Skilled positions in the aggregates industry pay a salary range of $50K–$90K, in a career that does not require a degree.
- Transportation alone can account for up to 70% of the delivered cost of materials.

## News & Updates

- [News & Insights](https://www.howtexasisbuilt.com/insights): Perspectives, data, and updates on how Texas is built — and the people and communities building it.
- [Take Action](https://www.howtexasisbuilt.com/take-action): Sign up for updates on how Texas is built and how you can help build a sustainable, resilient future.

## About

How Texas Is Built is an advocacy initiative of the Texas Aggregates & Concrete Association (TACA), the leading advocate for the aggregates, concrete, cement, and other associated industries in Texas. Learn more at [tx-taca.org](https://www.tx-taca.org/).
